# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I am the Blind monkey. I cannot see colors or read the manual, but I can feel the bomb and cut wires. I need to coordinate with Deaf (who sees) and Mute (who reads).

Since my previous gesture was rejected for using an invalid symbol (`👀` is not in the list), I must use only valid symbols from the provided alphabet. I want to signal to Deaf that I am ready to act based on their visual input, or perhaps ask them to point out a specific wire if they have identified one. However, without prior context, the safest first step is to establish a channel.

I will speak to Mute to ask for the rule regarding which wire to cut (e.g., "Cut the red wire" or "Cut the last wire").
I will gesture to Deaf using valid symbols to indicate "Wire" or "Cut". The alphabet has `✂️`? No. It has `👆`, `👇`, etc. Let's try to signal "Wait" or "Listen". Or simply acknowledge presence.
Actually, looking at the alphabet: `👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳`.

Let's try to ask Deaf to show me something about the wires. But I can't see gestures. Deaf receives my gestures. So I should gesture *to* Deaf to get their attention or convey a simple concept like "Yes/No" or "Point".
If I gesture `👆` (point up), Deaf might interpret it as "Look at the top?" or just a generic pointer.
If I gesture `🤝` (handshake), it might mean "Agreement" or "Help".

Let's stick to asking Mute for the primary directive via speech, as Mute can hear/read my speech. And send a simple gesture to Deaf to acknowledge I am listening/waiting for visual cues, or perhaps signaling "Cut" if we had agreed on a code. Since we haven't, I'll use `👋` (Wave) to say "Hello/I'm here" or `☝` (One finger) to signify "1st wire" or "Question".

Let's assume standard puzzle logic: I need to know which wire to cut.
To Mute: "What is the rule for cutting wires?"
To Deaf: Gesture `👆` pointing to myself? Or `✋` stop?
Let's try `👋` to Deaf to get attention.

```
speak(to="mute", text="What does the manual say about which wire to cut?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

Deaf says to Blind: Display shows 2. Light is yellow. There are 7 wires. Wire 1 is red. Wire 2 is white. Wire 3 is green. Wire 4 is yellow. Wire 5 is purple. Wire 6 is orange. Wire 7 is blue.

I am the Blind monkey. I have received a message from Deaf describing the bomb's visual state: Display shows 2, Light is yellow, and there are 7 wires with specific colors (1:Red, 2:White, 3:Green, 4:Yellow, 5:Purple, 6:Orange, 7:Blue).

I cannot see these colors or the display/light myself; I only know what Deaf told me. I need to consult Mute, who can read the manual, to determine which wire to cut based on this information. The manual likely contains rules linking the display number, light color, and wire colors to a specific action.

My plan:
1. Speak to Mute to relay the information from Deaf and ask for the correct procedure/wire to cut.
2. Since I don't have any new gestures to make that convey complex data without a pre-agreed code, and my primary need is textual instruction from Mute, I will focus on speaking. However, I must also send a gesture if possible or wait. The prompt says "You may send several messages...". I will speak to Mute. I will also gesture to Deaf to acknowledge receipt of their info, perhaps using `👍` (Yes/Good) to confirm I heard them.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: Display 2, Light Yellow. Wires: 1 Red, 2 White, 3 Green, 4 Yellow, 5 Purple, 6 Orange, 7 Blue. What does the manual say?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

Deaf says to Blind: Mute seems to be indicating the first item or wire. Please wait for further instructions from me.

I am the Blind monkey. I have received a message from Deaf stating that Mute is indicating the first item or wire, and Deaf asks me to wait for further instructions.

Since Deaf explicitly told me to wait, I should not cut any wires yet. However, I need to communicate with Mute to confirm what "the first item" refers to in the context of the manual's rules, as Mute cannot speak to me directly (Mute can only read). Wait, the rules say:
- Deaf sees bomb.
- Mute reads manual.
- Blind touches bomb.
- Speech goes to those who can hear. Gestures go to those who can see.

I am Blind. I can hear Mute? No, Mute is "Mute". Mute *reads* the manual but cannot speak. So Mute communicates via gestures? Or does Mute write things down? The prompt says "Mute... Cannot Speak". It doesn't explicitly say how Mute communicates, but usually in these puzzles, if someone can't speak, they might gesture or write. But I am Blind, so I can't see gestures or writing.

Let's re-read carefully.
"You are shown your own share at the start of every round..."
"Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words... A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was."
"Mute... Cannot Speak".
So Mute cannot send speech. Can Mute send gestures? Yes, anyone can gesture. But I am Blind, so I cannot receive gestures.
Therefore, I cannot receive information directly from Mute. I must rely on Deaf to interpret Mute's gestures and relay them to me via speech (since Deaf can speak/hear? The table says Deaf "Cannot Hear anything". So Deaf cannot hear me either!).

Wait.
Deaf: Sees bomb. Cannot hear. Cannot touch.
Mute: Reads manual. Cannot speak. Cannot touch.
Blind: Touches bomb. Cannot see.

Communication channels:
1. **Speech**: Only those who can hear receive it. Who can hear?
   - Deaf cannot hear.
   - Mute? The name implies no speech, but maybe hearing? Usually "Mute" means cannot speak, but can hear. Let's assume Mute can hear.
   - Blind? I am Blind. Can I hear? The prompt says "You never receive gesture." It doesn't say I can't hear. In fact, I just received text from Deaf ("Deaf says to Blind"). This implies Deaf *can* speak and I *can* hear.
   - If Deaf can speak, he must be able to produce sound. But the table says Deaf "Cannot Hear". It doesn't say he cannot speak.
   - If I can hear Deaf, then Deaf speaks to me.
   - Can I speak to Mute? If Mute can hear, yes.
   - Can Mute speak? No.
   - Can Mute gesture? Yes. Who sees gestures? Deaf and Blind? No, Blind cannot see. So only Deaf sees gestures.
   
   So the flow is likely:
   - Mute gestures -> Deaf sees -> Deaf speaks -> Blind hears -> Blind acts.
   - Blind speaks -> Mute hears (if Mute can hear) -> Mute reads manual -> Mute gestures -> Deaf sees -> Deaf speaks -> Blind hears.

   Current situation:
   Deaf said: "Mute seems to be indicating the first item or wire. Please wait for further instructions from me."
   
   This confirms Deaf is interpreting Mute's gestures. Deaf is telling me to wait.
   
   I should acknowledge this to Deaf? I can't gesture to Deaf because Deaf sees gestures. I can gesture. But Deaf said "wait".
   
   I should probably ask Mute (via speech, hoping Mute can hear) to clarify, OR just wait as instructed by Deaf. Since Deaf is the intermediary for visual info, and Deaf said wait, I will wait.
   
   However, I need to keep the channel open. I will speak to Mute to ask for clarification on "first item", assuming Mute can hear my speech. And I will gesture to Deaf to acknowledge receipt, using a standard symbol like `👌` (OK) or `✋` (Stop/Wait). Since Deaf asked me to wait, `✋` might be appropriate, or `👌` to confirm understanding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Clarify 'first item'. Is it Wire 1?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```
